subject: Renewal: term extension + capacity uplift — legal packet and sign-off timeline
messages:
From: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.com>
To: Emily Wang <emily@datumity.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@naomi_feldman.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 16:12:00 -0800
Subject: Renewal: term extension + capacity uplift — legal packet and sign-off timeline

Hi Emily —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Per our conversation, we put together the proposed paperwork for Datumity's renewal and the additional capacity uplift (increase from 3M to 5M tokens/month). Two items to highlight:

- Term: Datumity requested a 24-month renewal (instead of the current 12). We preliminarily accepted that subject to Legal review.
- Billing cadence: you preferred monthly invoicing with quarterly reconciliation; we flagged this for Finance.

Attached: the marked MSA with our in-line changes, and a draft Order Form (OrderForm_v3). We also included an SOC2 excerpt that procurement asked to see last quarter.

Can you confirm the final seat/license counts and whether procurement will provide a PO once the MSA language is agreed? If so, we can route for DocuSign this week — internal ask is to have Legal sign-off by EOD Friday so we can close before month-end.

Next steps from our side: Marissa will lead the commercial thread and Naomi will scope onboarding/technical kick-off. Kimberly, would you mind taking a first pass on the MSA notes below?

Thanks,
Lukas

--
Lukas Meyer
Senior Account Manager | Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 415 555 0198

From: Emily Wang <emily@datumity.com>

Cc: Alan Knox <alan.knox@datumity.com>, procurement@datumity.com
Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 09:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal: term extension + capacity uplift — legal packet and sign-off timeline

Lukas —

Thanks for sending these over. Quick clarifications from procurement:

- Capacity: confirm 5M tokens/month (burst to 7M allowed for first 30 days).
- PO: procurement will issue a PO once the attached MSA clean copy is received; prefer net-30 payment terms.
- Termination: our legal team prefers a 30-day termination for convenience with pro-rated refunds for unused prepaid credits. Is Redwood willing to accept this?

I've attached a short PO draft (PO_Datumity_2026.docx) for reference. If Redwood can accept a 24-month term and net-30, we can get the PO out within 48 hours of DocuSign.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — Emily

--
Emily Wang
Head of Procurement | Datumity Inc.
emily@datumity.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Emily Wang <emily@datumity.com>
Cc: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 11:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal: term extension + capacity uplift — legal packet and sign-off timeline

Emily — great, thanks for the PO draft. Two quick commercial points so Legal has context:

- We can confirm the 5M tokens/month baseline with a 30-day burst window to 7M for onboarding.
- Pricing: the uplift pricing used in OrderForm_v3 reflects a volume discount applied to the incremental tokens (line item 3).
- Net-30 is okay to propose, but Finance has asked to keep sample invoices tied to monthly usage reporting.

Kimberly — internal ask: can Legal advise on the termination clause and whether we accept a 30-day convenience termination with pro-rata refunds for unused prepaid credits? Also please check the new indemnity paragraph (page 6) and the data-retention section (page 9). Procurement wants SOC2 evidence attached (we included a recent excerpt).

Naomi — we'll need a short onboarding statement (SOW-lite) included as an attachment to the Order Form that lists milestone dates for the uplift — target kick-off: 2026-12-01. Can you draft that and drop it in the Drive link above?

Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, LegalOps <legal-ops@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 08:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal: term extension + capacity uplift — legal packet and sign-off timeline

Folks — I've reviewed the marked MSA and the Order Form. High-level guidance and redline direction below (we will produce a tracked PDF today):

1) Term / Termination:
- 24-month term: acceptable.
- 30-day convenience termination: we can accept for Datumity provided there is a pro-rated refund for any prepaid, unused credits and a minimum 60-day notice for any billing disputes to be eligible for refund. This protects Redwood from immediate churn during budgeting windows.

2) Liability / Indemnity / Warranty:
- Push back on broad warranty expansions. We'll keep the limited warranty language but accept a modest SLA credit (capped at 10% of monthly fees) for service outages beyond agreed SLOs.
- Keep liability cap at 12 months of fees for this customer; we will not accept uncapped consequential damages.

3) Data / Security Evidence:
- SOC2 excerpt included is fine as a starting point. Procurement requested the full report; we will provide a redactable SOC2 report via secure link (attach SOC2_excerpt_2026 for now). No changes to MSA needed beyond referencing the evidence package.

4) Sign-flow / DocuSign routing:
- Routing: Procurement signature (Datumity), Finance (Datumity), Redwood Sales (Marissa), Redwood Legal (kimberly.park@redwood.com), Redwood Ops (legal-ops@redwood.com).
- Please use the envelope title: "Datumity Renewal D-2026-1987" and route to legal-signature@redwood.com for final countersignature.

5) Timeline:
- I'll return a tracked MSA by EOD Thursday local time. If commercial accepts our modest edits, Legal can sign off and we can send final clean copy to DocuSign by Friday COB.

Action items: Marissa — confirm you accept the liability cap and the proposed SLA credit cap. Lukas — confirm DocuSign envelope details and point of contact at Datumity for signature routing. Naomi — drop SOW-lite into the Drive link so Legal can reference milestone dates.

Thanks,
Kimberly

--
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference

From: Emily Wang <emily@datumity.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Alan Knox <alan.knox@datumity.com>, procurement@datumity.com, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 6 Nov 2026 09:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal: term extension + capacity uplift — legal packet and sign-off timeline

Marissa / Lukas / Kimberly —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the clear guidance, Kimberly. Datumity is agreeable to the liability cap at 12 months and the SLA credit approach as described. Two small asks before we route to DocuSign:

1) One-time onboarding credit: Can Redwood include a one-time $20k onboarding credit (applied against first invoice) to help cover professional services for migration and validation?
2) Signature routing: please send the DocuSign envelope to emily@datumity.com and alan.knox@datumity.com — Alan will review with legal and countersign. Procurement (procurement@datumity.com) will upload the PO once signatures are complete.

If those two items are included, Datumity will approve the clean copy and we can be live with signatures by Friday afternoon. Please send the final clean MSA + Order Form and the DocuSign link when ready.

Best,
Emily

--
Emily Wang
Head of Procurement | Datumity Inc.
